title: First-order resolution: factoring and lifting ground proofs
summary: Unify selected relation literals, combine repeated pivots, and lift finite ground refutations to proofs with variables.
abstract: The requirements that every object satisfies a property and that a named object fails it contradict each other. Resolution finds this contradiction by substituting for variables until opposing relation statements agree. When several statements become the same after substitution, the rule must combine them before removing the opposing pair. We define this rule precisely, prove that it preserves truth in every structure, and show how every finite resolution proof using closed terms comes from a proof with variables. Herbrand's theorem then gives a finite refutation for every unsatisfiable set of universal clauses without equality, provided closed terms exist. Congruence axioms extend this conclusion to clauses with equality.

based_on.title: Logic for Computer Science: Foundations of Automatic Theorem Proving, Chapter 8 excerpt
